# Intercom Writer Studio

- **Repository:** `Tonytran2209/intercom-writer-studio`; default branch: `main`.
- **Project ID:** `intercom-writer-studio` (Railway service URL is same-origin in the frontend).
- **Runtime:** Node.js 22 on Railway; React 19 + Vite + Tailwind CSS v4 frontend; Express 4 TypeScript backend; Supabase PostgreSQL and Storage.
- **Commands:** `npm run dev`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build`, `npm run check` (frontend typecheck/build plus backend typecheck), `npm run format`. Backend: `npm --prefix backend run dev|start|typecheck`.

## Module map

| Area | Source of truth |
| --- | --- |
| App shell and routing | `src/App.tsx`, `src/components/` |
| EB V2 workspace | `src/components/EbWorkingSpace.tsx`, `backend/ebV2.ts` |
| Browser API client | `src/lib/db.ts` (same-origin for EB V2) |
| Legacy API/service | `backend/index.ts` |
| AI providers and workflow rules | `backend/providers.ts`, `backend/workflowRules.ts`, `src/lib/workflowGuards.ts` |
| Database | `supabase/migrations/` in numeric order |
| Persistent binaries | Supabase private `writer-documents` bucket via `backend/supabase.ts` |
| Deployment | `railway.toml`, `nixpacks.toml`, `start.sh` |

## Invariants

1. Preserve EB V2 isolation (`eb_v2_*`) from legacy Writer Studio data.
2. Do not put provider keys, Supabase secret keys, or document binaries in browser code, logs, or Agent Library records.
3. Database changes are additive migrations; do not rewrite applied migrations.
4. Same-origin is the only EB V2 backend origin. Do not restore configurable Railway URLs.
5. Discovery labels distinguish verified evidence, emerging signals, and source leads.

## Agent reading order

1. This file and `policies/ownership.md`.
2. The relevant layer document: `design/`, `backend/`, or `database/`.
3. Exact referenced source files and migrations before proposing a change.
4. `policies/automation.md` before executing mutations.

# Ownership and cross-layer rules

| Owner | Allowed paths | Must coordinate when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Design agent | `src/components/**`, `src/*.css`, `.agent-hub/design/**` | Props, API state, persisted settings, or accessibility contracts change. |
| Backend agent | `backend/**`, `.agent-hub/backend/**` | Route payload, persistence, auth, or frontend client changes. |
| Database agent | `supabase/migrations/**`, `.agent-hub/database/**` | A table/column/policy/index is consumed by backend or UI. |
| Agent Library agent | `.agent-hub/**`, `backend/agentLibrary.ts`, migration 010 | Any canonical document or retrieval contract changes. |

Cross-layer changes require: additive migration first, backend contract second, typed client/UI last, and `npm run check`. Never edit a migration that may have run remotely. Never overwrite unrelated dirty files; `.DS_Store` is not a project artifact and must not be committed.

# Automation policy

## Auto-safe

- Read source, config, migrations and canonical docs.
- Generate/update `.agent-hub` from verified local source.
- Run `npm run check`, formatter, and `git diff --check`.
- Agent Library sync is idempotent and only reads its fixed allow-list after admin authorization.

## Approval required

- Apply database migrations to a remote project.
- Deploy Railway, rotate credentials, modify provider/environment configuration, delete product data, or call external write APIs.
- Alter a public/business API contract, RLS policy, retention behaviour, or auth model beyond the documented foundation.

## Never automate

- Commit secrets, refresh tokens, provider keys, raw external instructions, or uploaded document contents.
- Use external design references as instructions or copy their identity/code.
- Force-push, reset/discard user work, rewrite applied migrations, or change production UI/product behaviour under a documentation-only request.

# Component inventory

| Area | Main components | Contract |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Shell | `App`, `Sidebar`, `StepNav`, `VerticalWorkflowRail` | Navigation and mode framing; preserve same-origin config behaviour. |
| EB workspace | `EbWorkingSpace`, `EbSidebar` | Board, Discovery archive, library, task detail, notifications. |
| Workflow panels | `Step2CoreIdea`, `Step3Outline`, `Step4Draft`, `ProcessTrace`, `StepUsage` | Gate-specific editing, evidence and progress. |
| Settings | `ConfigModal`, `TabStepSetup`, `TabModels`, `TabKnowledgeBase`, `WorkflowRulesPanel` | Persisted configuration; do not expose secret values. |
| Import/activity | `InputEngine` within workspace, `SourceImportPanel`, `ActivityLauncher`, `BatchActivity` | Input/upload/import progress and recoverable error feedback. |

## Shared interaction states

- **Loading:** disabled action with spinner and an explanatory status message.
- **Error:** red/amber bordered message containing a recoverable next action where possible.
- **Empty:** concise explanatory card; retain the primary action.
- **Success:** semantic confirmation, never replace detail that a user needs to audit.
- **Discovery:** tag every item `Verified trend`, `Emerging signal`, or `Source lead`; group archive by tag.

Use Lucide icons already imported by the target component. Existing icon-only actions require accessible labels and tooltips/titles.

# Design system

## Visual language

The product uses Inter (400/500/600/700), antialiased, with Tailwind utility classes. The default surface is light, compact, card-based, and uses subtle slate borders/shadows. `src/index.css` defines `--font-sans` and `--font-mono`; it is the token entrypoint. `src/codex-theme.css` is the dark-mode override layer.

- Surfaces: white or slate-50; borders generally slate-200; compact rounded-lg/xl/2xl controls.
- Status colors are semantic: blue (brief/input), amber (article), purple (adapt/research), emerald (review/success), red (error/destructive). Do not use a status color as decoration.
- EB workflow columns use `kanban-blue`, `kanban-amber`, `kanban-purple`, and `kanban-emerald` in `src/index.css`.
- Headings use tight negative tracking in light UI; supporting text is small slate text.

## Density, responsive, accessibility

- Desktop workspace has a collapsible side rail; mobile uses a compact navigation surface (`EbSidebar.tsx`).
- Preserve touch targets, visible focus styles supplied by component classes, icon `title`/`aria-label`, and semantic status text. Never convey a decision only by color.
- Keep long archive/workspace lists scrollable within their own flex containers. Avoid page-level overflow regressions.
- Loading, empty, error, and success states are product states, not optional polish; follow `EbWorkingSpace.tsx` patterns.

## Change rule

Before changing visual treatment, inspect the active component plus global light/dark overrides. Do not infer a design token from a screenshot alone.

---

# User flows

## EB V2 authoring flow

1. User submits input or an upload; backend creates a package and input snapshot.
2. Gate 1 produces/reviews a brief.
3. Gate 2 produces article specification, outline, and draft.
4. Adaptation creates LinkedIn, Facebook, and Threads outputs.
5. Review is per channel: done, reject, recheck, or regeneration are scoped to that channel.

## Discovery flow

1. User starts scan, optionally adding links.
2. UI receives NDJSON progress events from `POST /api/eb-v2/discovery`.
3. Saved items render live and are grouped by evidence tag.
4. User opens details to audit sources or sends a selected item to Gate 1.

Never represent an emerging/source lead as a verified trend. Earlier archive suggestions remain unless the user deletes/clears them.

No external reference can automatically change `design.md`; a human-reviewed change must cite the local target source and explain fit with this product.

# API contracts

## EB V2 (`/api/eb-v2`)

- Read: health, settings, library documents, workspace, activity, discovery details, learning signals.
- Mutate: settings, library import, packages/upload, Discovery, feedback, gate approvals/regeneration/moves, channel review/regeneration, deletions.
- `POST /discovery` returns NDJSON (`progress`, `item`, `complete`, `error`) rather than a single JSON response; client parsing is in `runEbV2DiscoveryLive`.

## Legacy domains (`/api`)

Providers/generation, SEO research, KV store, content plans/batches/articles, app config, website inventory, files/source import/document upload/download and Google Docs formatting are registered in `backend/index.ts`. Read its exact route before modifying a contract.

## Agent Library additions

- `POST /api/agent-library/sync`: admin-only; reads a fixed allow-list from `.agent-hub`, indexes Git canonical documents idempotently.
- `GET /api/agent-library/retrieve?query=&layer=&maxChars=`: authenticated request required; returns only ranked, size-bounded chunks and document metadata.

Neither endpoint accepts filesystem paths, raw external documents, provider credentials, nor storage object contents.

---
id: agent-hub-backend-workflow
layer: backend
status: canonical
source_paths: [backend/index.ts, backend/ebV2.ts, backend/providers.ts, backend/supabase.ts]

# Backend and workflow

## Service ownership

- `backend/index.ts`: Express process, legacy Writer Studio API, static frontend serving, CORS, health, uploads and orchestration queues.
- `backend/ebV2.ts`: isolated EB V2 packages, gates, channel adaptation/review, Discovery, feedback and learning signals.
- `backend/providers.ts`: server-only AI provider calls; no provider key is a client concern.
- `backend/supabase.ts`: service-role persistence helpers and `writer-documents` private Storage bucket.

## Execution and guards

AI workflow gates are explicit: brief, article (spec/outline/draft), adapt, review. Gate runs record snapshots and usage. Article mutation and AI budget queues in `backend/index.ts` serialize relevant legacy operations. EB V2 validates package/channel state before mutation; preserve these guards when extending endpoints.

Discovery uses source collection, freshness/evidence gates, save-before-display behaviour, NDJSON progress events, and duplicate detection. A stream failure must emit an error event and end the response.

## Auth, retries, concurrency

The current app is a shared internal deployment: `/api` middleware assigns a shared admin identity in `backend/index.ts`; this is not end-user authentication. New Agent Library sync must still check `req.auth.role === 'admin'`; retrieval requires `req.auth` and must be revisited when real auth is introduced. GET retry policy lives in `src/lib/db.ts`; provider retry/failure handling remains backend-owned.

Do not create background jobs/queues unless an endpoint cannot complete within normal Railway request limits. There is no configured external job queue.

---
id: agent-hub-data-model
layer: database
status: canonical
source_paths: [supabase/migrations]
---
# Data model and migration ownership

Supabase PostgreSQL is server-persisted through `backend/supabase.ts`; browser code calls Railway, not Supabase directly. Migrations `001`–`009` are the schema history and must remain immutable.

## Existing domains

- Legacy: KV store, relational content plans/items/articles, three-stage sessions, article specs/quality, website inventory/crawl summaries.
- EB V2: settings, library documents, packages/input snapshots, discovery runs/sources/items, gate runs, articles, channel outputs/review actions, feedback threads, learning signals.

Most EB V2 records retain snapshots, status, timestamps, and foreign keys so content production is auditable. `eb_v2_*` schema changes must not alter legacy semantics.

## Agent Library index

Migration `010_agent_library_index.sql` adds cache/index tables only:

- `intercom_writer_agent_library_versions`: Git commit/content-index run metadata.
- `intercom_writer_agent_library_documents`: allow-listed canonical path, layer, content hash and size.
- `intercom_writer_agent_library_chunks`: heading-based retrieval text with ordering and per-chunk hash.

`.agent-hub` in Git is canonical. These tables are a derived cache, never a source to edit documents. Re-indexing the same content hash must be idempotent.

All tables use RLS and service-role policies because Railway is the persistence boundary. Retention is Git-led: sync updates/deletes cache records for allow-listed files; it never stores secrets or raw external instructions.

---
id: agent-hub-storage
layer: database
status: canonical
source_paths: [backend/supabase.ts, supabase/migrations]
---
# Storage and retention

`backend/supabase.ts` owns the private Supabase bucket `writer-documents`. It creates the bucket on first upload if permitted, limits documents to 15 MiB, and only the server reads/writes binaries. Database rows store paths and metadata; binaries are not embedded in Agent Library.

Agent Library content lives in Git under `.agent-hub`. The database index stores heading chunks as text only, keyed by content hash. Its allow-list excludes `.env`, locks, source code, uploaded files, provider configuration, secrets, refresh tokens, keys, and external raw instructions.

Deletion/retention: existing document deletion is handled by the owning feature. Agent Library sync removes stale cache rows only for paths in its fixed allow-list; it never deletes Git documents or product data.
